content.text: Ordering at a Seafood Restaurant in 沖縄（うちなー）[Okinawa]
Suppose you go to a local area in Okinawa and not one of the more touristy places and you arrive to a local restaurant.
You might say something like, "[ordering item]、うにげーさびら", which the last word is a polite word for please (and the only one you need to know for now for the examination).
Once they deliver the food, they might say, うさがみそーれー, which is along the lines of like "Bon Appetit" and like "Enjoy your meal".
To this you can say, にふぇーろー or にふぇーどー, which means thanks (there are other variations in other dialects, but only these two are tested, which is used in the exact same way).
In reality, however, after you leave and the staff might say, "にふぇーでーびる" which is something more formal like "Thank you", and is used slightly more frequently unless talking to close friends.
